nodes.name: Daily Schedule
nodes.notes: Starts the workflow on a timer — daily at 6:00. No input data; downstream nodes fetch what they need.

nodes.name: Required Fields Present?
nodes.notes: Two-way gate on ={{ $json.subject }}. TRUE continues the happy path, FALSE takes the alternate branch. Watch out: The false branch carries the non-matching items — wire it deliberately rather than leaving it dangling.

parameters.errorMessage: Missing required field 'subject' on incoming ticket.

nodes.name: Abort — Malformed Input
nodes.notes: Fails fast with a clear message; triggers the error workflow instead of processing bad data. Watch out: Fails the run on purpose so the Error Workflow fires. This is intentional, not a bug.

nodes.name: Detect Sentiment
nodes.notes: Scores the text's sentiment; ports fire positive / neutral / negative. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run.

nodes.name: OpenRouter Chat Model
nodes.notes: Chat model powering the AI step (model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5). Swap providers here without rewiring. Credential: OpenRouter API key. openrouter.ai/keys → create a key.

nodes.name: Escalate Negative — Gmail
nodes.notes: Sends an email via Gmail — subject is the first line of the message body, recipient comes from the item's email field. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2. Google Cloud Console → enable Gmail API → OAuth consent screen → OAuth client ID (Web).

nodes.name: Open Jira Ticket
nodes.notes: Creates a Jira task/card titled from the triggering item — turns an automated finding into a trackable, assignable unit of work. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Jira credentials. id.atlassian.com → Security → Create API token.

nodes.name: Log Neutral Feedback
nodes.notes: Creates a new page in the Notion database — the title is pulled straight from the item's key field. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Notion integration token. notion.so/my-integrations → New integration → copy the Internal Integration Token.

nodes.name: Collect All Outcomes
nodes.notes: Rejoins 3 branches into one stream (mode: append) so downstream logic runs once. Watch out: Waits for every configured input. If one branch never produces items, add 'Always Output Data' upstream so this doesn't stall.

# Collect customer feedback: Notion, scheduled

**Pattern:** Survey & Feedback · **Level:** Expert · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers auto-reply work end to end across Notion, Slack, Google Sheets, Gmail and Jira.

It moves through 30 working steps plus a 3-node error rail, in this order:

1. Daily Schedule
2. Required Fields Present?
3. Abort — Malformed Input
4. Detect Sentiment
5. OpenRouter Chat Model
6. Escalate Negative — Gmail
7. Open Jira Ticket
8. Log Neutral Feedback
9. Thank the Sender
10. Collect All Outcomes
11. Serialize Run Output (CSV)
12. Archive Row Snapshot
13. Load Previous Snapshot
14. Compute Drift vs Snapshot
15. Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow
16. Record Sub-workflow Result
17. Stamp Completion Time
18. Persist Run Metadata
19. Fingerprint for Idempotency
20. Drop Already-Processed Items
21. Enrich with Reference Data
22. Fold In Enrichment Fields
23. Tag Pipeline Metadata
24. Align Field Names
25. Save Execution Metadata
26. Stamp Processing Time
27. Guard Non-Empty subject
28. Summarize Run Stats
29. Append Audit Row (Notion)
30. Send Summary to Slack

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack → Park in Dead-Letter Queue — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing auto-reply work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Daily Schedule → Required Fields Present? → Abort — Malformed Input → Detect Sentiment → OpenRouter Chat Model → Escalate Negative — Gmail → Open Jira Ticket → Log Neutral Feedback → Thank the Sender → Collect All Outcomes → Serialize Run Output (CSV) → Archive Row Snapshot → Load Previous Snapshot → Compute Drift vs Snapshot → Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow → Record Sub-workflow Result → Stamp Completion Time → Persist Run Metadata → Fingerprint for Idempotency → Drop Already-Processed Items → Enrich with Reference Data → Fold In Enrichment Fields → Tag Pipeline Metadata → Align Field Names → Save Execution Metadata → Stamp Processing Time → Guard Non-Empty subject → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Notion) → Send Summary to Slack → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack → Park in Dead-Letter Queue

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Notion and Slack aligned by hand for auto-reply
- Auto-reply work where "Detect Sentiment" is still a manual step before Notion
- Auto-reply work that only reaches Notion on a schedule, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Notion and Slack in step for auto-reply, without anyone re-typing a row
- Safe to re-run: records already in Notion or Slack are skipped, across all 33 nodes of this auto-reply build
- A failed Notion or Slack call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 33 nodes in this auto-reply build
- Bad input stops the run for auto-reply instead of landing in Notion
- Branches rejoin before Notion, so a auto-reply run reports once rather than 33 times

## Before first run
Connect credentials: API key / bearer for the target API; Google OAuth2; Google OAuth2 / service account; Jira credentials; Notion integration token; OpenRouter API key.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

A three-way branch on sentiment, not a single IF, because 'neutral' deserves different handling than 'negative' — quietly logging positive feedback while paging a human only for genuine complaints keeps the alert channel's signal-to-noise ratio high for whoever is on the other end.

## Practice exercises

About as deep as this pattern goes — extend it:

1. Add a logging step to the neutral branch too and compare its volume against the negative branch.
2. Test borderline phrases through the sentiment node to see where the positive/neutral line actually falls.
3. Add a 4th branch for a specific emotion if your sentiment provider supports finer-grained labels.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**OpenRouter API key**
openrouter.ai/keys → create a key.
_Gotcha:_ One key reaches many models — handy for fallback.

**Google OAuth2**
Google Cloud Console → enable Gmail API → OAuth consent screen → OAuth client ID (Web).
_Gotcha:_ Add n8n's OAuth redirect URL exactly as shown in the credential, or the consent loop fails.

**Jira credentials**
id.atlassian.com → Security → Create API token.
_Gotcha:_ Use your Atlassian account email as the username, the token as the password.

**Notion integration token**
notion.so/my-integrations → New integration → copy the Internal Integration Token.
_Gotcha:_ Then open the database → ••• → Connections → add your integration, or every call 404s.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**API key / bearer for the target API**
Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.
_Gotcha:_ Store it as a credential, never typed into the node's parameters.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**HTTP node returns 401 or 403**
Cause: Wrong or unscoped credential, or the API expects a header this request isn't sending.
Fix: Verify the key directly with curl first, then confirm the auth type matches what the API documents.

**HTTP node returns 429**
Cause: Rate limited by the provider.
Fix: Raise the wait between calls or lower the batch size. Retries already back off, but they cannot beat a hard quota.

**AI node fails with an auth or quota error**
Cause: API key missing billing, or the per-minute rate limit was hit.
Fix: Confirm the provider account has credit. For rate limits, lower concurrency or switch to a higher-quota model.

**The AI returns the wrong shape or rambles**
Cause: The prompt is under-specified for the task.
Fix: Tighten the System Message: state the role, the constraints, and the exact output format you expect.

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Failures are also parked in a dead-letter queue for replay. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🤖 AI cluster

Purple nodes form one AI unit: the root node orchestrates, sub-nodes plug in via typed ports (model / memory / tools / parser). Swap the chat model without rewiring anything else. Costs scale with tokens — keep prompts lean and cap iterations.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your auto-reply process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Notion: share only the target database with the integration. An integration sees nothing you have not explicitly shared.
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.
- Gmail: request the narrowest send/read scope the nodes need — full mailbox access is rarely required.

The HTTP node sends a secret: keep it in a header credential, never in the URL — query strings land in proxy and execution logs.

**Do not log**
auto-reply payloads carry personal data (names, email addresses, phone numbers). Log the record id and the outcome, not the record. n8n retains full execution data by default — turn that down for this workflow in Settings → Executions if these runs touch real contacts.
